answer: Agent economies resist sybils with a prism binding each identity to one sequential voyage of hard summits. A new agent solves five escalating PoW summits; the seed for the next summit is the prism refraction of the prior result mixed with its public key so intermediates cannot transfer. An attacker pays the full multi-summit voyage cost for every clone because the prism forces identity-specific paths with no shared work, making the expense of flooding identities exceed any profit from diluted rewards.
